verses.decoded: And David said to Uriah, Go down to your house and wash your feet. And Uriah left the king’s house, and a meal from the king was sent after him.

verses.kjv: But Uriah slept at the door of the king’s house with all the servants of his lord, and went not down to his house.
verses.decoded: But Uriah slept at the entrance of the king’s house with all the servants of his master, and he did not go down to his own house.

verses.kjv: And when they had told David, saying, Uriah went not down unto his house, David said unto Uriah, Camest thou not from thy journey? why then didst thou not go down unto thine house?
verses.decoded: When they told David, saying, Uriah did not go to his house, David asked Uriah, "Did you not come back from your journey? Why then did you not go to your house?"

verses.kjv: And Uriah said unto David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open fields; shall I then go into mine house, to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? as thou livest, and as thy soul liveth, I will not do this thing.
verses.decoded: And Uriah said to David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah are staying in tents; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are camped in the open fields; should I then go into my house, to eat and drink, and lie with my wife? As you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do this thing.

verses.kjv: And David said to Uriah, Tarry here to day also, and to morrow I will let thee depart. So Uriah abode in Jerusalem that day, and the morrow.
verses.decoded: And David said to Uriah, Stay here today as well, and tomorrow I will let you leave. So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next.

verses.kjv: And when David had called him, he did eat and drink before him; and he made him drunk: and at even he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but went not down to his house.
verses.decoded: When David called him, he ate and drank in front of David; and David made him drunk. In the evening, he went out to lie on his bed with his master's servants, but he did not go down to his own house.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass in the morning, that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
verses.decoded: The next morning, David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it with Uriah.

verses.kjv: And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.
verses.decoded: And he wrote in the letter, saying, Place Uriah at the front of the fiercest battle, and then pull back from him so that he will be struck down and die.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when Joab observed the city, that he assigned Uriah unto a place where he knew that valiant men were.
verses.decoded: When Joab watched the city, he sent Uriah to a place where he knew brave soldiers were stationed.

verses.kjv: And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and there fell some of the people of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.
verses.decoded: The men from the city came out and fought against Joab, and some of the soldiers serving David were killed; Uriah the Hittite also died.

verses.kjv: Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;
verses.decoded: Then Joab sent a message to David and told him everything about the war;

verses.kjv: And charged the messenger, saying, When thou hast made an end of telling the matters of the war unto the king,
verses.decoded: And instructed the messenger, saying, When you have finished reporting the details of the war to the king,

verses.kjv: And if so be that the king’s wrath arise, and he say unto thee, Wherefore approached ye so nigh unto the city when ye did fight? knew ye not that they would shoot from the wall?
verses.decoded: And if the king becomes angry and asks you, 'Why did you come so close to the city when you were fighting? Didn't you know they would shoot from the wall?'

verses.kjv: Who smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from the wall, that he died in Thebez? why went ye nigh the wall? then say thou, Thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
verses.decoded: Who killed Abimelech, the son of Jerubbesheth? Wasn't it a woman who threw a piece of a millstone at him from the wall, causing him to die in Thebez? Why did you come near the wall? Then say, 'Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.'

verses.kjv: So the messenger went, and came and shewed David all that Joab had sent him for.
verses.decoded: So the messenger went and came back and told David everything that Joab had sent him to report.

verses.kjv: And the messenger said unto David, Surely the men prevailed against us, and came out unto us into the field, and we were upon them even unto the entering of the gate.
verses.decoded: And the messenger said to David, The men definitely defeated us and came out to meet us in the field, and we fought against them all the way to the entrance of the gate.

verses.kjv: And the shooters shot from off the wall upon thy servants; and some of the king’s servants be dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
verses.decoded: The archers shot from the wall at your servants; some of the king’s servants have died, and your servant Uriah the Hittite has also died.

verses.kjv: Then David said unto the messenger, Thus shalt thou say unto Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sword devoureth one as well as another: make thy battle more strong against the city, and overthrow it: and encourage thou him.
verses.decoded: Then David said to the messenger, Say this to Joab, Do not let this upset you, because the sword kills one person as well as another: make your attack stronger against the city, and destroy it; and encourage him.

verses.kjv: And when the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she mourned for her husband.
verses.decoded: When Uriah's wife heard that her husband Uriah was dead, she grieved for him.

verses.kjv: And when the mourning was past, David sent and fetched her to his house, and she became his wife, and bare him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased the Lord.
verses.decoded: After the mourning period ended, David sent for her and brought her to his house. She became his wife and gave birth to a son. However, what David had done was displeasing to the LORD.

verses.kjv: And the Lord sent Nathan unto David. And he came unto him, and said unto him, There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.
verses.decoded: The LORD sent Nathan to David. Nathan went to him and said, "There were two men in the same city; one was rich, and the other was poor."

verses.kjv: The rich man had exceeding many flocks and herds:
verses.decoded: The rich man owned a very large number of sheep and cattle.

verses.kjv: But the poor man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished up: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own meat, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was unto him as a daughter.
verses.decoded: But the poor man had nothing except one little female lamb, which he had bought and raised; it grew up with him and his children; it ate from his own food, drank from his own cup, lay in his arms, and was like a daughter to him.

verses.kjv: And there came a traveller unto the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to dress for the wayfaring man that was come unto him; but took the poor man’s lamb, and dressed it for the man that was come to him.
verses.decoded: A traveler came to the rich man, and he refused to take from his own flock or herd to prepare food for the traveler who had come to him; instead, he took the poor man’s lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him.

verses.kjv: And David’s anger was greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, As the Lord liveth, the man that hath done this thing shall surely die:
verses.decoded: And David became very angry with the man; and he said to Nathan, As the LORD lives, the man who has done this thing will definitely die:

verses.kjv: And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.
verses.decoded: He will pay back four times as much for the lamb, because he did this and had no mercy.

verses.kjv: And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;
verses.decoded: And Nathan said to David, You are the man. This is what the LORD God of Israel says: I anointed you king over Israel, and I rescued you from the hand of Saul;

verses.kjv: And I gave thee thy master’s house, and thy master’s wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that had been too little, I would moreover have given unto thee such and such things.
verses.decoded: And I gave you your master's house, and your master's wives to be with you, and I gave you the kingdom of Israel and Judah; and if that had been too little, I would have given you even more.

verses.kjv: Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment of the Lord, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon.
verses.decoded: Why have you rejected the command of the LORD by doing evil in His sight? You have killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, taken his wife to be your wife, and killed him with the sword of the Ammonites.

verses.kjv: Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.
verses.decoded: Now, the sword will never leave your family because you have rejected me and taken Uriah the Hittite's wife to be your wife.

verses.kjv: Thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house, and I will take thy wives before thine eyes, and give them unto thy neighbour, and he shall lie with thy wives in the sight of this sun.
verses.decoded: This is what the LORD says: Look, I will bring disaster against you from your own family. I will take your wives in front of you and give them to your neighbor, and he will sleep with your wives in broad daylight.

verses.kjv: For thou didst it secretly: but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.
verses.decoded: Because you did this secretly, I will do this thing openly before all Israel and in broad daylight.

verses.kjv: And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the Lord. And Nathan said unto David, The Lord also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.
verses.decoded: And David said to Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD. And Nathan said to David, The LORD has also forgiven your sin; you will not die.

verses.kjv: Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the Lord to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die.
verses.decoded: However, because you have caused the enemies of the LORD to speak evil because of this action, the child born to you will certainly die.

verses.kjv: And Nathan departed unto his house. And the Lord struck the child that Uriah’s wife bare unto David, and it was very sick.
verses.decoded: And Nathan went back to his house. The LORD caused the child that Uriah’s wife gave birth to David to become very sick.

verses.kjv: David therefore besought God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night upon the earth.
verses.decoded: David asked God earnestly for the child; and David fasted, then went inside and lay on the ground all night.

verses.kjv: And the elders of his house arose, and went to him, to raise him up from the earth: but he would not, neither did he eat bread with them.
verses.decoded: The elders of his household stood up and went to him to help him get up from the ground, but he refused and did not eat bread with them.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead: for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he would not hearken unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead?
verses.decoded: On the seventh day, the child died. David's servants were afraid to tell him that the child had died because they said, Look, while the child was still alive, we spoke to him, and he would not listen to our voice. How much more will he be upset if we tell him that the child is dead?

verses.kjv: But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: therefore David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.
verses.decoded: But when David saw that his servants were whispering, he realized that the child was dead. So David asked his servants, "Is the child dead?" And they said, "He is dead."

verses.kjv: Then David arose from the earth, and washed, and anointed himself, and changed his apparel, and came into the house of the Lord, and worshipped: then he came to his own house; and when he required, they set bread before him, and he did eat.
verses.decoded: Then David got up from the ground, washed himself, put on oil, changed his clothes, and went into the house of the LORD to worship. After that, he went to his own house, and when he asked, they gave him bread, and he ate.

verses.kjv: Then said his servants unto him, What thing is this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and weep for the child, while it was alive; but when the child was dead, thou didst rise and eat bread.
verses.decoded: Then his servants said to him, What is this thing you have done? You fasted and wept for the child while it was alive, but after the child died, you got up and ate food.

verses.kjv: And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who can tell whether God will be gracious to me, that the child may live?
verses.decoded: And he said, While the child was still alive, I fasted and cried because I thought, Who can know if God will be kind to me so that the child might live?

verses.kjv: But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me.
verses.decoded: But now that he is dead, why should I continue to fast? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not come back to me.

verses.kjv: And David comforted Bath-sheba his wife, and went in unto her, and lay with her: and she bare a son, and he called his name Solomon: and the Lord loved him.
verses.decoded: David comforted Bath-sheba his wife, and he went to her and slept with her. She gave birth to a son, and he named him Solomon. The LORD loved him.

verses.kjv: And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, because of the Lord.
verses.decoded: He sent Nathan the prophet to name him Jedidiah, because of the LORD.

verses.kjv: And Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.
verses.decoded: Joab fought against Rabbah, the city of the Ammonites, and captured the royal city.

verses.kjv: And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, I have fought against Rabbah, and have taken the city of waters.
verses.decoded: And Joab sent messengers to David and said, I have fought against Rabbah and have captured the city of waters.

verses.kjv: Now therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city, and take it: lest I take the city, and it be called after my name.
verses.decoded: So now, gather the remaining people together, camp outside the city, and capture it; otherwise, I will capture the city myself, and it will be named after me.

verses.kjv: And David gathered all the people together, and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and took it.
verses.decoded: David gathered all the people together, went to Rabbah, fought against it, and captured it.

verses.kjv: And he took their king’s crown from off his head, the weight whereof was a talent of gold with the precious stones: and it was set on David’s head. And he brought forth the spoil of the city in great abundance.
verses.decoded: He took the king's crown off his head, which weighed about a talent of gold and was decorated with precious stones, and placed it on David's head. He also brought out a large amount of treasure from the city.

verses.kjv: And he brought forth the people that were therein, and put them under saws, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brickkiln: and thus did he unto all the cities of the children of Ammon. So David and all the people returned unto Jerusalem.
verses.decoded: He brought out the people who were there and put them under saws, iron harrows, and iron axes, and made them pass through the brick kiln. He did this to all the cities of the children of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass after this, that Absalom the son of David had a fair sister, whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.
verses.decoded: After this happened, Absalom, the son of David, had a beautiful sister named Tamar; and Amnon, the son of David, loved her.

verses.kjv: And Amnon was so vexed, that he fell sick for his sister Tamar; for she was a virgin; and Amnon thought it hard for him to do any thing to her.
verses.decoded: Amnon was so upset that he became sick because of his sister Tamar; she was a virgin; and Amnon found it difficult to do anything to her.

verses.kjv: But Amnon had a friend, whose name was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David’s brother: and Jonadab was a very subtil man.
verses.decoded: But Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David’s brother; and Jonadab was a very clever man.

verses.kjv: And he said unto him, Why art thou, being the king’s son, lean from day to day? wilt thou not tell me? And Amnon said unto him, I love Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.
verses.decoded: And he said to him, Why are you, being the king’s son, getting thinner every day? Won’t you tell me? And Amnon said to him, I love Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.

verses.kjv: And Jonadab said unto him, Lay thee down on thy bed, and make thyself sick: and when thy father cometh to see thee, say unto him, I pray thee, let my sister Tamar come, and give me meat, and dress the meat in my sight, that I may see it, and eat it at her hand.
verses.decoded: And Jonadab said to him, Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick; and when your father comes to see you, say to him, Please let my sister Tamar come and bring me some food, and prepare the food in front of me, so that I can see it and eat it from her hand.

verses.kjv: So Amnon lay down, and made himself sick: and when the king was come to see him, Amnon said unto the king, I pray thee, let Tamar my sister come, and make me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat at her hand.
verses.decoded: So Amnon lay down and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, Please let my sister Tamar come and make me two cakes in front of me, so I can eat them from her hand.

verses.kjv: Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, Go now to thy brother Amnon’s house, and dress him meat.
verses.decoded: Then David sent a message to Tamar, saying, Go now to your brother Amnon’s house, and prepare food for him.

verses.kjv: So Tamar went to her brother Amnon’s house; and he was laid down. And she took flour, and kneaded it, and made cakes in his sight, and did bake the cakes.
verses.decoded: So Tamar went to her brother Amnon’s house; he was lying down. She took flour, kneaded it, made cakes in front of him, and baked the cakes.

verses.kjv: And she took a pan, and poured them out before him; but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, Have out all men from me. And they went out every man from him.
verses.decoded: She took a pan and poured the food out in front of him, but he refused to eat. Then Amnon said, "Everyone leave me." So all the men left him.

verses.kjv: And Amnon said unto Tamar, Bring the meat into the chamber, that I may eat of thine hand. And Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them into the chamber to Amnon her brother.
verses.decoded: And Amnon said to Tamar, Bring the food into the room so I can eat from your hand. And Tamar took the cakes she had made and brought them into the room to Amnon her brother.

verses.kjv: And when she had brought them unto him to eat, he took hold of her, and said unto her, Come lie with me, my sister.
verses.decoded: And when she had brought them to him to eat, he grabbed her and said to her, Come lie with me, my sister.

verses.kjv: And she answered him, Nay, my brother, do not force me; for no such thing ought to be done in Israel: do not thou this folly.
verses.decoded: And she answered him, No, my brother, do not force me; because nothing like this should be done in Israel: do not do this foolish thing.

verses.kjv: And I, whither shall I cause my shame to go? and as for thee, thou shalt be as one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, I pray thee, speak unto the king; for he will not withhold me from thee.
verses.decoded: And I, where can I take my shame? And as for you, you will be like one of the fools in Israel. Now, please, speak to the king, because he will not refuse me to you.

verses.kjv: Howbeit he would not hearken unto her voice: but, being stronger than she, forced her, and lay with her.
verses.decoded: However, he did not listen to her voice; but, being stronger than her, he forced her and slept with her.

verses.kjv: Then Amnon hated her exceedingly; so that the hatred wherewith he hated her was greater than the love wherewith he had loved her. And Amnon said unto her, Arise, be gone.
verses.decoded: Then Amnon hated her very much; the hatred he felt for her was stronger than the love he had for her. And Amnon said to her, Get up and leave.

verses.kjv: And she said unto him, There is no cause: this evil in sending me away is greater than the other that thou didst unto me. But he would not hearken unto her.
verses.decoded: And she said to him, There is no reason: this harm in sending me away is worse than the other harm you did to me. But he did not listen to her.

verses.kjv: Then he called his servant that ministered unto him, and said, Put now this woman out from me, and bolt the door after her.
verses.decoded: Then he called his servant who served him and said, Take this woman away from me and lock the door behind her.

verses.kjv: And she had a garment of divers colours upon her: for with such robes were the king’s daughters that were virgins apparelled. Then his servant brought her out, and bolted the door after her.
verses.decoded: She was wearing a garment of many colors because the king’s virgin daughters were dressed in such robes. Then his servant brought her out and locked the door behind her.

verses.kjv: And Tamar put ashes on her head, and rent her garment of divers colours that was on her, and laid her hand on her head, and went on crying.
verses.decoded: And Tamar put ashes on her head, tore the multicolored garment she was wearing, placed her hand on her head, and kept crying.

verses.kjv: And Absalom her brother said unto her, Hath Amnon thy brother been with thee? but hold now thy peace, my sister: he is thy brother; regard not this thing. So Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom’s house.
verses.decoded: And Absalom, her brother, said to her, "Has Amnon, your brother, been with you? But now be quiet, my sister; he is your brother; do not pay attention to this matter." So Tamar stayed alone in her brother Absalom’s house.

verses.kjv: But when king David heard of all these things, he was very wroth.
verses.decoded: But when King David heard about all these things, he became very angry.

verses.kjv: And Absalom spake unto his brother Amnon neither good nor bad: for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar.
verses.decoded: And Absalom did not say anything good or bad to his brother Amnon, because Absalom hated Amnon since he had raped his sister Tamar.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass after two full years, that Absalom had sheepshearers in Baal-hazor, which is beside Ephraim: and Absalom invited all the king’s sons.
verses.decoded: After two full years, Absalom had sheep shearing at Baal-hazor, which is near Ephraim, and Absalom invited all the king’s sons.

verses.kjv: And Absalom came to the king, and said, Behold now, thy servant hath sheepshearers; let the king, I beseech thee, and his servants go with thy servant.
verses.decoded: And Absalom came to the king and said, Look now, your servant has sheep shearers; please let the king and his servants go with your servant.

verses.kjv: And the king said to Absalom, Nay, my son, let us not all now go, lest we be chargeable unto thee. And he pressed him: howbeit he would not go, but blessed him.
verses.decoded: And the king said to Absalom, No, my son, let us not all go now, so that we do not become a burden to you. But he urged him; however, he would not go, but blessed him.

verses.kjv: Then said Absalom, If not, I pray thee, let my brother Amnon go with us. And the king said unto him, Why should he go with thee?
verses.decoded: Then Absalom said, If not, please let my brother Amnon go with us. And the king said to him, Why should he go with you?

verses.kjv: But Absalom pressed him, that he let Amnon and all the king’s sons go with him.
verses.decoded: But Absalom insisted that he allow Amnon and all the king’s sons to go with him.

verses.kjv: Now Absalom had commanded his servants, saying, Mark ye now when Amnon’s heart is merry with wine, and when I say unto you, Smite Amnon; then kill him, fear not: have not I commanded you? be courageous, and be valiant.
verses.decoded: Now Absalom had commanded his servants, saying, Watch carefully when Amnon’s heart is happy with wine, and when I tell you, Strike Amnon; then kill him. Do not be afraid. Have I not commanded you? Be brave and strong.

verses.kjv: And the servants of Absalom did unto Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king’s sons arose, and every man gat him up upon his mule, and fled.
verses.decoded: And Absalom's servants did to Amnon exactly as Absalom had ordered. Then all the king's sons got up, and each one mounted his mule and ran away.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, while they were in the way, that tidings came to David, saying, Absalom hath slain all the king’s sons, and there is not one of them left.
verses.decoded: While they were traveling, news came to David saying, Absalom has killed all the king’s sons, and not one of them is left.

verses.kjv: Then the king arose, and tare his garments, and lay on the earth; and all his servants stood by with their clothes rent.
verses.decoded: Then the king got up, tore his clothes, and lay down on the ground; and all his servants stood nearby with their clothes torn.

verses.kjv: And Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David’s brother, answered and said, Let not my lord suppose that they have slain all the young men the king’s sons; for Amnon only is dead: for by the appointment of Absalom this hath been determined from the day that he forced his sister Tamar.
verses.decoded: Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David’s brother, answered and said, Do not think, my lord, that all the king’s sons have been killed; only Amnon is dead. This was planned by Absalom from the day he raped his sister Tamar.

verses.kjv: Now therefore let not my lord the king take the thing to his heart, to think that all the king’s sons are dead: for Amnon only is dead.
verses.decoded: So now, my lord the king, please do not be upset and think that all the king’s sons are dead; only Amnon is dead.

verses.kjv: But Absalom fled. And the young man that kept the watch lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, there came much people by the way of the hill side behind him.
verses.decoded: But Absalom ran away. The young man who was on guard looked up and saw many people coming along the hillside road behind him.

verses.kjv: And Jonadab said unto the king, Behold, the king’s sons come: as thy servant said, so it is.
verses.decoded: And Jonadab said to the king, Look, the king’s sons are coming: just as your servant said, it is so.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, as soon as he had made an end of speaking, that, behold, the king’s sons came, and lifted up their voice and wept: and the king also and all his servants wept very sore.
verses.decoded: It happened that as soon as he finished speaking, the king’s sons came, raised their voices, and cried; the king and all his servants also cried very much.

verses.kjv: But Absalom fled, and went to Talmai, the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And David mourned for his son every day.
verses.decoded: But Absalom ran away and went to Talmai, the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And David grieved for his son every day.

verses.kjv: So Absalom fled, and went to Geshur, and was there three years.
verses.decoded: So Absalom ran away and went to Geshur, and stayed there for three years.

verses.kjv: And the soul of king David longed to go forth unto Absalom: for he was comforted concerning Amnon, seeing he was dead.
verses.decoded: King David deeply wanted to go out to Absalom because he was comforted about Amnon, since he was dead.

verses.kjv: Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart was toward Absalom.
verses.decoded: Now Joab, the son of Zeruiah, realized that the king favored Absalom.

verses.kjv: And Joab sent to Tekoah, and fetched thence a wise woman, and said unto her, I pray thee, feign thyself to be a mourner, and put on now mourning apparel, and anoint not thyself with oil, but be as a woman that had a long time mourned for the dead:
verses.decoded: And Joab sent to Tekoah and brought a wise woman from there, and said to her, Please pretend to be a mourner, put on mourning clothes now, do not anoint yourself with oil, but act like a woman who has mourned for the dead for a long time.

verses.kjv: And come to the king, and speak on this manner unto him. So Joab put the words in her mouth.
verses.decoded: Go to the king and speak to him like this. So Joab gave her the words to say.

verses.kjv: And when the woman of Tekoah spake to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, and did obeisance, and said, Help, O king.
verses.decoded: When the woman from Tekoah spoke to the king, she fell face down on the ground, bowed deeply, and said, Help me, King.

verses.kjv: And the king said unto her, What aileth thee? And she answered, I am indeed a widow woman, and mine husband is dead.
verses.decoded: And the king said to her, What is wrong with you? And she answered, I am truly a widow, and my husband is dead.

verses.kjv: And thy handmaid had two sons, and they two strove together in the field, and there was none to part them, but the one smote the other, and slew him.
verses.decoded: Your servant woman had two sons, and the two of them were fighting together in the field, and no one was there to separate them, but one struck the other and killed him.

verses.kjv: And, behold, the whole family is risen against thine handmaid, and they said, Deliver him that smote his brother, that we may kill him, for the life of his brother whom he slew; and we will destroy the heir also: and so they shall quench my coal which is left, and shall not leave to my husband neither name nor remainder upon the earth.
verses.decoded: Look, the entire family has risen up against your servant, and they said, 'Hand over the one who struck his brother so we can kill him, to avenge the life of the brother he killed; and we will also destroy the heir.' In this way, they will put out the fire that is left of me and will not leave any name or descendants for my husband on the earth.

verses.kjv: And the king said unto the woman, Go to thine house, and I will give charge concerning thee.
verses.decoded: And the king said to the woman, Go to your house, and I will give instructions about you.

verses.kjv: And the woman of Tekoah said unto the king, My lord, O king, the iniquity be on me, and on my father’s house: and the king and his throne be guiltless.
verses.decoded: The woman from Tekoah said to the king, My lord, O king, let the sin be on me and on my father's family; but let the king and his throne be innocent.

verses.kjv: And the king said, Whosoever saith ought unto thee, bring him to me, and he shall not touch thee any more.
verses.decoded: And the king said, Whoever says anything to you, bring him to me, and he will not harm you anymore.

verses.kjv: Then said she, I pray thee, let the king remember the Lord thy God, that thou wouldest not suffer the revengers of blood to destroy any more, lest they destroy my son. And he said, As the Lord liveth, there shall not one hair of thy son fall to the earth.
verses.decoded: Then she said, I ask you, let the king remember the LORD your God, so that you will not allow the avengers of blood to kill any more, or else they will kill my son. And he said, As the LORD lives, not one hair of your son will fall to the ground.

verses.kjv: Then the woman said, Let thine handmaid, I pray thee, speak one word unto my lord the king. And he said, Say on.
verses.decoded: Then the woman said, Please let your servant speak one word to my lord the king. And he said, Go ahead.

verses.kjv: And the woman said, Wherefore then hast thou thought such a thing against the people of God? for the king doth speak this thing as one which is faulty, in that the king doth not fetch home again his banished.
verses.decoded: And the woman said, Why have you thought such a thing against the people of God? For the king speaks like someone who is wrong, because the king does not bring back his banished people.

verses.kjv: For we must needs die, and are as water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; neither doth God respect any person: yet doth he devise means, that his banished be not expelled from him.
verses.decoded: For we all have to die, and we are like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; God does not show favoritism to anyone: yet he plans ways so that those who are banished are not completely cut off from him.

verses.kjv: Now therefore that I am come to speak of this thing unto my lord the king, it is because the people have made me afraid: and thy handmaid said, I will now speak unto the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his handmaid.
verses.decoded: Now that I have come to speak about this matter to my lord the king, it is because the people have frightened me; and your servant said, I will now speak to the king; maybe the king will grant the request of his servant.

verses.kjv: For the king will hear, to deliver his handmaid out of the hand of the man that would destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.
verses.decoded: Because the king will listen and rescue his servant woman from the man who wants to destroy me and my son together from God's inheritance.

verses.kjv: Then thine handmaid said, The word of my lord the king shall now be comfortable: for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and bad: therefore the Lord thy God will be with thee.
verses.decoded: Then your servant woman said, The word of my lord the king will now be comforting: because like an angel of God, my lord the king is able to understand good and bad: therefore the LORD your God will be with you.

verses.kjv: Then the king answered and said unto the woman, Hide not from me, I pray thee, the thing that I shall ask thee. And the woman said, Let my lord the king now speak.
verses.decoded: Then the king answered and said to the woman, Please do not hide from me the thing I am going to ask you. And the woman said, Let my lord the king speak now.

verses.kjv: And the king said, Is not the hand of Joab with thee in all this? And the woman answered and said, As thy soul liveth, my lord the king, none can turn to the right hand or to the left from ought that my lord the king hath spoken: for thy servant Joab, he bade me, and he put all these words in the mouth of thine handmaid:
verses.decoded: The king said, "Is Joab involved with you in all of this?" The woman answered, "As surely as you live, my lord the king, no one can turn right or left from anything my lord the king has said. Your servant Joab told me to do this, and he put all these words in my mouth."

verses.kjv: To fetch about this form of speech hath thy servant Joab done this thing: and my lord is wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are in the earth.
verses.decoded: To bring about this kind of speech, your servant Joab has done this thing: and my lord is wise, with the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are on the earth.

verses.kjv: And the king said unto Joab, Behold now, I have done this thing: go therefore, bring the young man Absalom again.
verses.decoded: And the king said to Joab, Look, I have done this thing: go now, bring the young man Absalom back.

verses.kjv: And Joab fell to the ground on his face, and bowed himself, and thanked the king: and Joab said, To day thy servant knoweth that I have found grace in thy sight, my lord, O king, in that the king hath fulfilled the request of his servant.
verses.decoded: And Joab fell to the ground on his face, bowed himself, and thanked the king. Joab said, Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your sight, my lord, O king, because the king has fulfilled the request of his servant.

verses.kjv: So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
verses.decoded: So Joab got up and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom back to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And the king said, Let him turn to his own house, and let him not see my face. So Absalom returned to his own house, and saw not the king’s face.
verses.decoded: And the king said, Let him go back to his own house, and do not let him see my face. So Absalom returned to his own house and did not see the king’s face.

verses.kjv: But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.
verses.decoded: But in all Israel, no one was praised as much as Absalom for his beauty: from the bottom of his foot to the top of his head, there was no flaw in him.

verses.kjv: And when he polled his head, (for it was at every year’s end that he polled it: because the hair was heavy on him, therefore he polled it:) he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels after the king’s weight.
verses.decoded: And when he cut his hair, (because he cut it at the end of every year: since his hair was heavy on him, he cut it:) he weighed the hair from his head at two hundred shekels according to the king’s weight.

verses.kjv: And unto Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar: she was a woman of a fair countenance.
verses.decoded: Absalom had three sons and one daughter named Tamar; she was a woman with a beautiful appearance.

verses.kjv: So Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem, and saw not the king’s face.
verses.decoded: So Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two full years and did not see the king's face.

verses.kjv: Therefore Absalom sent for Joab, to have sent him to the king; but he would not come to him: and when he sent again the second time, he would not come.
verses.decoded: So Absalom sent for Joab to send him to the king, but Joab did not come to him; and when Absalom sent again a second time, Joab still did not come.

verses.kjv: Therefore he said unto his servants, See, Joab’s field is near mine, and he hath barley there; go and set it on fire. And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.
verses.decoded: So he said to his servants, Look, Joab’s field is close to mine, and he has barley there; go and set it on fire. And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.

verses.kjv: Then Joab arose, and came to Absalom unto his house, and said unto him, Wherefore have thy servants set my field on fire?
verses.decoded: Then Joab got up and went to Absalom's house and said to him, Why have your servants set my field on fire?

verses.kjv: And Absalom answered Joab, Behold, I sent unto thee, saying, Come hither, that I may send thee to the king, to say, Wherefore am I come from Geshur? it had been good for me to have been there still: now therefore let me see the king’s face; and if there be any iniquity in me, let him kill me.
verses.decoded: And Absalom answered Joab, Look, I sent to you, saying, Come here, so that I could send you to the king to say, Why did I come back from Geshur? It would have been better for me to still be there. Now, let me see the king’s face, and if there is any wrongdoing in me, let him kill me.

verses.kjv: So Joab came to the king, and told him: and when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king, and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king: and the king kissed Absalom.
verses.decoded: So Joab went to the king and told him. When the king called for Absalom, he came to the king and bowed his face to the ground before him. Then the king kissed Absalom.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass after this, that Absalom prepared him chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him.
verses.decoded: After this, Absalom got chariots and horses ready for himself, along with fifty men to run ahead of him.

verses.kjv: And Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate: and it was so, that when any man that had a controversy came to the king for judgment, then Absalom called unto him, and said, Of what city art thou? And he said, Thy servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.
verses.decoded: And Absalom got up early and stood by the road near the gate. Whenever someone who had a dispute came to the king for judgment, Absalom would call to him and ask, "What city are you from?" And the man would say, "I am a servant from one of the tribes of Israel."

verses.kjv: And Absalom said unto him, See, thy matters are good and right; but there is no man deputed of the king to hear thee.
verses.decoded: And Absalom said to him, Look, your cases are good and fair; but there is no man appointed by the king to listen to you.

verses.kjv: Absalom said moreover, Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man which hath any suit or cause might come unto me, and I would do him justice!
verses.decoded: Absalom also said, "I wish I were appointed judge in the land, so that anyone who has a dispute or case could come to me, and I would give them justice!"

verses.kjv: And it was so, that when any man came nigh to him to do him obeisance, he put forth his hand, and took him, and kissed him.
verses.decoded: And it happened that when anyone came near him to show respect, he reached out his hand, took him, and kissed him.

verses.kjv: And on this manner did Absalom to all Israel that came to the king for judgment: so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
verses.decoded: And Absalom did this to all the people of Israel who came to the king for judgment: in this way, Absalom won the hearts of the men of Israel.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass after forty years, that Absalom said unto the king, I pray thee, let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed unto the Lord, in Hebron.
verses.decoded: After forty years, Absalom said to the king, "Please let me go and fulfill the vow I made to the LORD in Hebron."

verses.kjv: For thy servant vowed a vow while I abode at Geshur in Syria, saying, If the Lord shall bring me again indeed to Jerusalem, then I will serve the Lord.
verses.decoded: Because your servant made a promise while I was living in Geshur in Syria, saying, If the LORD truly brings me back to Jerusalem, then I will serve the LORD.

verses.kjv: And the king said unto him, Go in peace. So he arose, and went to Hebron.
verses.decoded: And the king said to him, Go in peace. So he got up and went to Hebron.

verses.kjv: But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, As soon as ye hear the sound of the trumpet, then ye shall say, Absalom reigneth in Hebron.
verses.decoded: But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then you shall say, Absalom is reigning in Hebron.

verses.kjv: And with Absalom went two hundred men out of Jerusalem, that were called; and they went in their simplicity, and they knew not any thing.
verses.decoded: And with Absalom went two hundred men from Jerusalem, who were called; and they went without suspicion, and they did not know anything.

verses.kjv: And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counseller, from his city, even from Giloh, while he offered sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong; for the people increased continually with Absalom.
verses.decoded: And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s advisor, from his city, Giloh, while he was offering sacrifices. The conspiracy was strong because more and more people kept joining Absalom.

verses.kjv: And there came a messenger to David, saying, The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.
verses.decoded: A messenger came to David and said, The people of Israel are supporting Absalom.

verses.kjv: And David said unto all his servants that were with him at Jerusalem, Arise, and let us flee; for we shall not else escape from Absalom: make speed to depart, lest he overtake us suddenly, and bring evil upon us, and smite the city with the edge of the sword.
verses.decoded: And David said to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem, Get up, and let us flee; because we will not escape from Absalom otherwise: hurry to leave, so that he does not catch us suddenly, and bring disaster upon us, and strike the city with the sword.

verses.kjv: And the king’s servants said unto the king, Behold, thy servants are ready to do whatsoever my lord the king shall appoint.
verses.decoded: And the king’s servants said to the king, Look, your servants are ready to do whatever my lord the king commands.

verses.kjv: And the king went forth, and all his household after him. And the king left ten women, which were concubines, to keep the house.
verses.decoded: The king went out, and all his household followed him. The king left ten women, who were his concubines, to take care of the palace.

verses.kjv: And the king went forth, and all the people after him, and tarried in a place that was far off.
verses.decoded: The king went out, and all the people followed him, and stayed in a place that was far away.

verses.kjv: And all his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men which came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.
verses.decoded: All his servants walked beside him; and all the Cherethites, all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who followed him from Gath, walked in front of the king.

verses.kjv: Then said the king to Ittai the Gittite, Wherefore goest thou also with us? return to thy place, and abide with the king: for thou art a stranger, and also an exile.
verses.decoded: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, Why are you also going with us? Return to your place and stay with the king, because you are a foreigner and also an exile.

verses.kjv: Whereas thou camest but yesterday, should I this day make thee go up and down with us? seeing I go whither I may, return thou, and take back thy brethren: mercy and truth be with thee.
verses.decoded: Since you only came yesterday, should I make you go up and down with us today? Because I am going wherever I can, you go back and bring your brothers with you. May kindness and truth be with you.

verses.kjv: And Ittai answered the king, and said, As the Lord liveth, and as my lord the king liveth, surely in what place my lord the king shall be, whether in death or life, even there also will thy servant be.
verses.decoded: And Ittai answered the king and said, As the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, surely wherever my lord the king is, whether in death or life, there your servant will also be.

verses.kjv: And David said to Ittai, Go and pass over. And Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones that were with him.
verses.decoded: And David said to Ittai, Go and cross over. And Ittai the Gittite crossed over, along with all his men and all the children who were with him.

verses.kjv: And all the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over: the king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over, toward the way of the wilderness.
verses.decoded: And everyone in the land cried out loudly, and all the people crossed over; the king himself also crossed over the Kidron brook, and all the people crossed over toward the wilderness road.

verses.kjv: And lo Zadok also, and all the Levites were with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God: and they set down the ark of God; and Abiathar went up, until all the people had done passing out of the city.
verses.decoded: And look, Zadok and all the Levites were with him, carrying the ark of the covenant of God. They put down the ark of God, and Abiathar went up until all the people had finished leaving the city.

verses.kjv: And the king said unto Zadok, Carry back the ark of God into the city: if I shall find favour in the eyes of the Lord, he will bring me again, and shew me both it, and his habitation:
verses.decoded: And the king said to Zadok, Take the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, he will bring me back and show me both the ark and his dwelling place.

verses.kjv: But if he thus say, I have no delight in thee; behold, here am I, let him do to me as seemeth good unto him.
verses.decoded: But if he says, 'I have no pleasure in you,' here I am; let him do to me whatever he thinks is right.

verses.kjv: The king said also unto Zadok the priest, Art not thou a seer? return into the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz thy son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.
verses.decoded: The king also said to Zadok the priest, Are you not a prophet? Return to the city in peace, and take your two sons with you, Ahimaaz your son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.

verses.kjv: See, I will tarry in the plain of the wilderness, until there come word from you to certify me.
verses.decoded: Look, I will stay in the plain of the wilderness until I receive a message from you to inform me.

verses.kjv: Zadok therefore and Abiathar carried the ark of God again to Jerusalem: and they tarried there.
verses.decoded: Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem, and they stayed there.

verses.kjv: And David went up by the ascent of mount Olivet, and wept as he went up, and had his head covered, and he went barefoot: and all the people that was with him covered every man his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.
verses.decoded: And David went up the slope of Mount Olivet, crying as he went up, with his head covered and his feet bare; and all the people with him covered their heads, and they went up, crying as they went up.

verses.kjv: And one told David, saying, Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom. And David said, O Lord, I pray thee, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.
verses.decoded: Someone told David, saying, Ahithophel is among the people plotting with Absalom. And David said, O LORD, I ask you, make Ahithophel's advice foolish.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that when David was come to the top of the mount, where he worshipped God, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat rent, and earth upon his head:
verses.decoded: It happened that when David reached the top of the mountain, where he worshiped God, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat torn and dust on his head.

verses.kjv: Unto whom David said, If thou passest on with me, then thou shalt be a burden unto me:
verses.decoded: David said to him, If you continue to go with me, then you will be a burden to me.

verses.kjv: But if thou return to the city, and say unto Absalom, I will be thy servant, O king; as I have been thy father’s servant hitherto, so will I now also be thy servant: then mayest thou for me defeat the counsel of Ahithophel.
verses.decoded: But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'I will be your servant, O king; just as I have been your father’s servant until now, I will now also be your servant,' then you may defeat Ahithophel’s advice for me.

verses.kjv: And hast thou not there with thee Zadok and Abiathar the priests? therefore it shall be, that what thing soever thou shalt hear out of the king’s house, thou shalt tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
verses.decoded: Do you not have Zadok and Abiathar the priests with you there? So, whatever you hear from the king’s house, you must tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.

verses.kjv: Behold, they have there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz Zadok’s son, and Jonathan Abiathar’s son; and by them ye shall send unto me every thing that ye can hear.
verses.decoded: Look, they have their two sons with them there, Ahimaaz son of Zadok, and Jonathan son of Abiathar; and through them you will send me everything you hear.

verses.kjv: So Hushai David’s friend came into the city, and Absalom came into Jerusalem.
verses.decoded: So Hushai, David’s friend, entered the city, and Absalom entered Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And when David was a little past the top of the hill, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, with a couple of asses saddled, and upon them two hundred loaves of bread, and an hundred bunches of raisins, and an hundred of summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.
verses.decoded: When David had just passed the top of the hill, Ziba, the servant of Mephibosheth, met him with two saddled donkeys carrying two hundred loaves of bread, one hundred bunches of raisins, one hundred pieces of dried fruit, and a bottle of wine.

verses.kjv: And the king said unto Ziba, What meanest thou by these? And Ziba said, The asses be for the king’s household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine, that such as be faint in the wilderness may drink.
verses.decoded: And the king said to Ziba, What do you mean by these? And Ziba said, The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat; and the wine is for those who are weak in the wilderness to drink.

verses.kjv: And the king said, And where is thy master’s son? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he abideth at Jerusalem: for he said, To day shall the house of Israel restore me the kingdom of my father.
verses.decoded: And the king said, Where is your master's son? And Ziba said to the king, Look, he is staying in Jerusalem because he said, Today the people of Israel will give me back my father's kingdom.

verses.kjv: Then said the king to Ziba, Behold, thine are all that pertained unto Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, I humbly beseech thee that I may find grace in thy sight, my lord, O king.
verses.decoded: Then the king said to Ziba, Look, everything that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours. And Ziba said, I earnestly ask that I may find favor in your eyes, my lord, O king.

verses.kjv: And when king David came to Bahurim, behold, thence came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed still as he came.
verses.decoded: When King David arrived at Bahurim, a man from the family of Saul named Shimei, the son of Gera, came out. He came forward and kept cursing as he went.

verses.kjv: And he cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David: and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.
verses.decoded: He threw stones at David and at all the servants of King David, while all the people and all the strong men were on his right side and on his left side.

verses.kjv: And thus said Shimei when he cursed, Come out, come out, thou bloody man, and thou man of Belial:
verses.decoded: And Shimei said this when he cursed, Come out, come out, you bloody man, and you worthless man:

verses.kjv: The Lord hath returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned; and the Lord hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son: and, behold, thou art taken in thy mischief, because thou art a bloody man.
verses.decoded: The LORD has brought back on you all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned; and the LORD has given the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son: and look, you are caught in your own wrongdoing, because you are a violent man.

verses.kjv: Then said Abishai the son of Zeruiah unto the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.
verses.decoded: Then Abishai, the son of Zeruiah, said to the king, Why should this worthless man curse my lord the king? Please let me go over and cut off his head.

verses.kjv: And the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, because the Lord hath said unto him, Curse David. Who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so?
verses.decoded: And the king said, What do I have to do with you, sons of Zeruiah? Let him curse, because the LORD told him, 'Curse David.' Who then can say, 'Why have you done this?'

verses.kjv: And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, which came forth of my bowels, seeketh my life: how much more now may this Benjamite do it? let him alone, and let him curse; for the Lord hath bidden him.
verses.decoded: And David said to Abishai and all his servants, Look, my own son, who came from my body, is trying to take my life; how much more now might this Benjamite do it? Leave him alone and let him curse, because the LORD has told him to.

verses.kjv: It may be that the Lord will look on mine affliction, and that the Lord will requite me good for his cursing this day.
verses.decoded: It is possible that the LORD will notice my suffering, and that the LORD will repay me with good for the curse he spoke against me today.

verses.kjv: And as David and his men went by the way, Shimei went along on the hill’s side over against him, and cursed as he went, and threw stones at him, and cast dust.
verses.decoded: As David and his men were traveling along the road, Shimei walked on the hillside opposite them, shouting insults as he went, throwing stones at David, and throwing dust.

verses.kjv: And the king, and all the people that were with him, came weary, and refreshed themselves there.
verses.decoded: The king and all the people with him arrived tired and rested there.

verses.kjv: And Absalom, and all the people the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.
verses.decoded: Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel came with him.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David’s friend, was come unto Absalom, that Hushai said unto Absalom, God save the king, God save the king.
verses.decoded: It happened that when Hushai the Archite, David’s friend, came to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, 'May God protect the king, may God protect the king.'

verses.kjv: And Absalom said to Hushai, Is this thy kindness to thy friend? why wentest thou not with thy friend?
verses.decoded: And Absalom said to Hushai, Is this how you show kindness to your friend? Why didn't you go with your friend?

verses.kjv: And Hushai said unto Absalom, Nay; but whom the Lord, and this people, and all the men of Israel, choose, his will I be, and with him will I abide.
verses.decoded: And Hushai said to Absalom, No; but I will be the one whom the LORD, this people, and all the men of Israel choose, and I will stay with him.

verses.kjv: And again, whom should I serve? should I not serve in the presence of his son? as I have served in thy father’s presence, so will I be in thy presence.
verses.decoded: And again, whom should I serve? Should I not serve in the presence of his son? Just as I have served in your father’s presence, I will serve in your presence.

verses.kjv: Then said Absalom to Ahithophel, Give counsel among you what we shall do.
verses.decoded: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Discuss among yourselves what we should do."

verses.kjv: And Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Go in unto thy father’s concubines, which he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then shall the hands of all that are with thee be strong.
verses.decoded: And Ahithophel said to Absalom, Go to your father’s concubines, whom he has left to take care of the house; and all Israel will hear that you are hated by your father: then everyone who is with you will be encouraged.

verses.kjv: So they spread Absalom a tent upon the top of the house; and Absalom went in unto his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
verses.decoded: So they set up a tent for Absalom on the roof of the house; and Absalom went to his father’s concubines in front of all Israel.

verses.kjv: And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had inquired at the oracle of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.
verses.decoded: The advice that Ahithophel gave at that time was like someone asking God for guidance. This was true for all the advice Ahithophel gave to both David and Absalom.

verses.kjv: Moreover Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Let me now choose out twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David this night:
verses.decoded: Also Ahithophel said to Absalom, Let me now select twelve thousand men, and I will get up and chase after David tonight:

verses.kjv: And I will come upon him while he is weary and weak handed, and will make him afraid: and all the people that are with him shall flee; and I will smite the king only:
verses.decoded: I will attack him when he is tired and weak, and I will cause him to be afraid; all the people with him will run away, and I will strike only the king.

verses.kjv: And I will bring back all the people unto thee: the man whom thou seekest is as if all returned: so all the people shall be in peace.
verses.decoded: And I will bring all the people back to you: the man you are looking for is as if everyone has returned: so all the people will be at peace.

verses.kjv: And the saying pleased Absalom well, and all the elders of Israel.
verses.decoded: And the advice pleased Absalom very much, and all the leaders of Israel.

verses.kjv: Then said Absalom, Call now Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likewise what he saith.
verses.decoded: Then Absalom said, Call Hushai the Archite now, and let us also hear what he says.

verses.kjv: And when Hushai was come to Absalom, Absalom spake unto him, saying, Ahithophel hath spoken after this manner: shall we do after his saying? if not; speak thou.
verses.decoded: When Hushai came to Absalom, Absalom said to him, "Ahithophel has given this advice: should we follow his advice? If not, then you speak."

verses.kjv: And Hushai said unto Absalom, The counsel that Ahithophel hath given is not good at this time.
verses.decoded: And Hushai said to Absalom, The advice that Ahithophel has given is not good right now.

verses.kjv: For, said Hushai, thou knowest thy father and his men, that they be mighty men, and they be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field: and thy father is a man of war, and will not lodge with the people.
verses.decoded: For, said Hushai, you know your father and his men, that they are mighty men, and they are angry in their minds, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the field; and your father is a man of war, and will not stay with the people.

verses.kjv: Behold, he is hid now in some pit, or in some other place: and it will come to pass, when some of them be overthrown at the first, that whosoever heareth it will say, There is a slaughter among the people that follow Absalom.
verses.decoded: Look, he is now hidden in some pit or in another place; and it will happen that when some of them are defeated at first, whoever hears about it will say, There is a massacre among the people who follow Absalom.

verses.kjv: And he also that is valiant, whose heart is as the heart of a lion, shall utterly melt: for all Israel knoweth that thy father is a mighty man, and they which be with him are valiant men.
verses.decoded: And even the brave man, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will completely lose courage; because all Israel knows that your father is a powerful man, and those who are with him are brave men.

verses.kjv: Therefore I counsel that all Israel be generally gathered unto thee, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude; and that thou go to battle in thine own person.
verses.decoded: Therefore, I advise that all Israel be gathered to you from Dan to Beer-sheba, as numerous as the sand by the sea; and that you go to battle in person.

verses.kjv: So shall we come upon him in some place where he shall be found, and we will light upon him as the dew falleth on the ground: and of him and of all the men that are with him there shall not be left so much as one.
verses.decoded: Then we will find him somewhere he can be found, and we will come upon him like dew falling on the ground; and not one of him or all the men with him will be left alive.

verses.kjv: Moreover, if he be gotten into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city, and we will draw it into the river, until there be not one small stone found there.
verses.decoded: Furthermore, if he gets into a city, then all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will pull it into the river until not even a small stone is left there.

verses.kjv: And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For the Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the Lord might bring evil upon Absalom.
verses.decoded: And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The advice of Hushai the Archite is better than the advice of Ahithophel. Because the LORD had planned to frustrate the good advice of Ahithophel, so that the LORD might bring disaster on Absalom.

verses.kjv: Then said Hushai unto Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus did Ahithophel counsel Absalom and the elders of Israel; and thus and thus have I counselled.
verses.decoded: Then Hushai said to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, This is the advice Ahithophel gave to Absalom and the elders of Israel; and this is the advice I have given.

verses.kjv: Now therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, Lodge not this night in the plains of the wilderness, but speedily pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that are with him.
verses.decoded: So now send a message quickly to David, saying, Do not stay tonight in the open fields of the wilderness, but cross over quickly; otherwise the king and all the people with him might be destroyed.

verses.kjv: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed by En-rogel; for they might not be seen to come into the city: and a wench went and told them; and they went and told king David.
verses.decoded: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed near En-rogel because they could not be seen entering the city. A young woman went and told them, and they went and told King David.

verses.kjv: Nevertheless a lad saw them, and told Absalom: but they went both of them away quickly, and came to a man’s house in Bahurim, which had a well in his court; whither they went down.
verses.decoded: However, a young boy saw them and told Absalom; but both of them left quickly and went to a man's house in Bahurim, which had a well in its courtyard; they went down into it.

verses.kjv: And the woman took and spread a covering over the well’s mouth, and spread ground corn thereon; and the thing was not known.
verses.decoded: The woman took a covering and placed it over the well's opening, then spread ground corn on top of it; no one noticed what she did.

verses.kjv: And when Absalom’s servants came to the woman to the house, they said, Where is Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said unto them, They be gone over the brook of water. And when they had sought and could not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.decoded: When Absalom’s servants came to the woman’s house, they asked, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered them, “They have crossed the stream.” After searching and not finding them, they returned to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, after they were departed, that they came up out of the well, and went and told king David, and said unto David, Arise, and pass quickly over the water: for thus hath Ahithophel counselled against you.
verses.decoded: After they left, they came up out of the well and went to tell King David, saying to David, 'Get up and quickly cross the water, because Ahithophel has given this advice against you.'

verses.kjv: Then David arose, and all the people that were with him, and they passed over Jordan: by the morning light there lacked not one of them that was not gone over Jordan.
verses.decoded: Then David got up, and all the people who were with him, and they crossed over the Jordan River: by morning light, not one of them was missing; all had crossed over the Jordan.

verses.kjv: And when Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his ass, and arose, and gat him home to his house, to his city, and put his household in order, and hanged himself, and died, and was buried in the sepulchre of his father.
verses.decoded: When Ahithophel saw that his advice was not accepted, he saddled his donkey, got up, went back to his house in his city, arranged his household, hanged himself, died, and was buried in his father's tomb.

verses.kjv: Then David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom passed over Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.
verses.decoded: Then David arrived at Mahanaim. And Absalom crossed the Jordan River, along with all the men of Israel who were with him.

verses.kjv: And Absalom made Amasa captain of the host instead of Joab: which Amasa was a man’s son, whose name was Ithra an Israelite, that went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah Joab’s mother.
verses.decoded: And Absalom made Amasa commander of the army instead of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra, an Israelite, who was married to Abigail, the daughter of Nahash, who was the sister of Zeruiah, Joab’s mother.

verses.kjv: So Israel and Absalom pitched in the land of Gilead.
verses.decoded: So Israel and Absalom set up camp in the land of Gilead.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when David was come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
verses.decoded: When David arrived at Mahanaim, Shobi, the son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, Machir, the son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim,

verses.kjv: Brought beds, and basons, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and parched corn, and beans, and lentiles, and parched pulse,
verses.decoded: They brought beds, and basins, and clay pots, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and roasted grain, and beans, and lentils, and roasted legumes,

verses.kjv: And honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of kine, for David, and for the people that were with him, to eat: for they said, The people is hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness.
verses.decoded: And honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese made from cows, for David and for the people who were with him to eat; because they said, The people are hungry, tired, and thirsty in the wilderness.

verses.kjv: And David numbered the people that were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.
verses.decoded: David counted the people who were with him and appointed commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds over them.

verses.kjv: And David sent forth a third part of the people under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said unto the people, I will surely go forth with you myself also.
verses.decoded: David sent one-third of the people under the command of Joab, one-third under the command of Abishai, the son of Zeruiah and Joab’s brother, and one-third under the command of Ittai the Gittite. The king said to the people, "I will definitely go out with you myself as well."

verses.kjv: But the people answered, Thou shalt not go forth: for if we flee away, they will not care for us; neither if half of us die, will they care for us: but now thou art worth ten thousand of us: therefore now it is better that thou succour us out of the city.
verses.decoded: But the people answered, You must not go out, because if we run away, they will not care about us; even if half of us die, they will not care about us. But now you are worth ten thousand of us, so it is better for you to rescue us from the city.

verses.kjv: And the king said unto them, What seemeth you best I will do. And the king stood by the gate side, and all the people came out by hundreds and by thousands.
verses.decoded: And the king said to them, Whatever you think is best, I will do. And the king stood by the gate, and all the people came out in hundreds and thousands.

verses.kjv: And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Deal gently for my sake with the young man, even with Absalom. And all the people heard when the king gave all the captains charge concerning Absalom.
verses.decoded: The king gave orders to Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, saying, Be gentle for my sake with the young man, Absalom. All the people heard the king give these instructions to all the commanders about Absalom.

verses.kjv: So the people went out into the field against Israel: and the battle was in the wood of Ephraim;
verses.decoded: So the people went out into the field to fight against Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.

verses.kjv: Where the people of Israel were slain before the servants of David, and there was there a great slaughter that day of twenty thousand men.
verses.decoded: The people of Israel were killed in front of David's servants, and there was a huge killing that day of twenty thousand men.

verses.kjv: For the battle was there scattered over the face of all the country: and the wood devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.
verses.decoded: Because the battle was spread out across the entire region, and the forest killed more people that day than the sword did.

verses.kjv: And Absalom met the servants of David. And Absalom rode upon a mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that was under him went away.
verses.decoded: Absalom met David's servants. Absalom was riding a mule, and the mule went under the thick branches of a large oak tree. His head got caught in the tree, and he was hanging between the sky and the ground, while the mule he was riding went away.

verses.kjv: And a certain man saw it, and told Joab, and said, Behold, I saw Absalom hanged in an oak.
verses.decoded: A man saw it and told Joab, saying, I saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree.

verses.kjv: And Joab said unto the man that told him, And, behold, thou sawest him, and why didst thou not smite him there to the ground? and I would have given thee ten shekels of silver, and a girdle.
verses.decoded: And Joab said to the man who told him, "You saw him, so why did you not strike him down right there? I would have given you ten shekels of silver and a belt."

verses.kjv: And the man said unto Joab, Though I should receive a thousand shekels of silver in mine hand, yet would I not put forth mine hand against the king’s son: for in our hearing the king charged thee and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Beware that none touch the young man Absalom.
verses.decoded: And the man said to Joab, Even if I were given a thousand shekels of silver in my hand, I still would not reach out my hand against the king’s son; because we heard the king tell you, Abishai, and Ittai, 'Be careful that no one harms the young man Absalom.'

verses.kjv: Otherwise I should have wrought falsehood against mine own life: for there is no matter hid from the king, and thou thyself wouldest have set thyself against me.
verses.decoded: Otherwise I would have done something harmful to my own life, because nothing is hidden from the king, and you yourself would have opposed me.

verses.kjv: Then said Joab, I may not tarry thus with thee. And he took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak.
verses.decoded: Then Joab said, I cannot delay like this with you. And he took three spears in his hand and stabbed them through Absalom's heart while he was still alive in the middle of the oak tree.

verses.kjv: And ten young men that bare Joab’s armour compassed about and smote Absalom, and slew him.
verses.decoded: And ten young men who carried Joab’s armor surrounded Absalom, struck him, and killed him.

verses.kjv: And Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel: for Joab held back the people.
verses.decoded: And Joab blew the trumpet, and the soldiers stopped chasing Israel because Joab stopped them.

verses.kjv: And they took Absalom, and cast him into a great pit in the wood, and laid a very great heap of stones upon him: and all Israel fled every one to his tent.
verses.decoded: They took Absalom and threw him into a large pit in the forest, then piled a huge heap of stones on top of him. All of Israel then went back to their own tents.

verses.kjv: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself a pillar, which is in the king’s dale: for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance: and he called the pillar after his own name: and it is called unto this day, Absalom’s place.
verses.decoded: During his lifetime, Absalom had taken and set up a pillar for himself in the king’s valley, because he said, 'I have no son to keep my name alive.' He named the pillar after himself, and it is still called Absalom’s place today.

verses.kjv: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, Let me now run, and bear the king tidings, how that the Lord hath avenged him of his enemies.
verses.decoded: Then Ahimaaz, the son of Zadok, said, "Let me run now and bring the king the news of how the LORD has avenged him against his enemies."

verses.kjv: And Joab said unto him, Thou shalt not bear tidings this day, but thou shalt bear tidings another day: but this day thou shalt bear no tidings, because the king’s son is dead.
verses.decoded: And Joab said to him, You will not bring news today, but you will bring news another day: today you will bring no news, because the king’s son is dead.
